answer: Behavioural drift scoring. Each identity’s action vector is compared across epochs against a kernel of its own past patterns, and a sustained drift beyond a saffron threshold triggers quarantine. The rule works by requiring each identity to stay within a fixed ridge of behavioural distance from its own prior epoch, so copied agents diverge as their handlers adapt. An attacker must maintain long-lived, internally consistent histories per fake identity, multiplying operational cost by the number of epochs enforced.
